deep.reconstruction:
This is a scratch page. It is written upside down on the back of a mainframe printout whose header is IBM JCL (EXEC PGM=IEFBR14) submitting a job to a 'CRAY2', with job id J0424CNU. Two things are on it.

(1) A small group-theoretic computation. Take a cyclic sequence of involutions σ_0, σ_1, …, σ_{N-1}, indices mod N (σ_N = σ_0), with σ_i^2 = 1. Define the consecutive products ρ_i = σ_{i-1}σ_i, so ρ_1 = σ_0σ_1, ρ_2 = σ_1σ_2, …, ρ_N = σ_{N-1}σ_N = σ_{N-1}σ_0. Then ρ_1ρ_2 = σ_0σ_2, and the products telescope, giving ρ_1ρ_2…ρ_k = σ_0σ_k and finally ρ_1…ρ_N = σ_0σ_N = σ_0^2 = 1. This is the standard picture of rotations as products of two reflections, as in a dihedral or Coxeter group. The composite of the transitions around a closed cycle of positions is trivial whenever each transition factors as two consecutive involutions.

In context, the neighbouring pages discuss gluing the complexes Δ*_D, Δ*_{D'} when a pseudo-line D is swept over a vertex. They ask whether the gluing iso should be 'parallel transport' or its opposite, and they track orientations ω_F → ω_D → ω_{D'} around circuits that surround 'superposi-singular' positions. The computation is therefore a check of orientation monodromy. If each elementary move acts on orientations as a product of two involutions (e.g. antipody / orientation reversals), the holonomy around a circuit of N moves is trivial. A sign discrepancy, like the one found on the next page with 'parallel transport', has to come from a transition that is not of this form.

(2) Sketches of pseudo-line arrangements:
- pencils of lines through marked points, in the 'star' configurations of the previous page;
- a polygon (hexagon) triangulated from a central point, with an overlaid zigzag cell structure, i.e. a cell/zonotopal-type picture of the circuit of arrangement types around a vertex;
- a small count, roughly '(n-1)-(N-1)-(N-1)-(N'-1)' and 'n-r', apparently counting cells or lines.
errors: No error in the telescoping identity itself. Note that ρ_i^2 = 1 does not hold in general (ρ_i^2 = σ_{i-1}σ_iσ_{i-1}σ_i). If the illegible line asserts ρ_i^2 = 1, it would need σ_{i-1} and σ_i to commute; the natural reading is ρ_1…ρ_N = 1.

ideas.what: Consecutive products of a cyclic chain of involutions telescope to the identity around the cycle; used to control orientation monodromy of gluings around circuits of pseudo-line arrangement moves
ideas.modern_name: Rotations as products of reflections / Coxeter-type relation; trivial holonomy of an orientation local system

ideas.what: Picture of the cycle of arrangement types around a vertex as a subdivided polygon (hexagon) with a cell structure
ideas.modern_name: Higher Bruhat order / cellular structure of the space of pseudo-line arrangements (zonotopal tilings)

missed.claim: Dating evidence. The paper is a printout of a JCL job addressed to a 'CRAY2' from an IBM MVS front end, job id ending 'CNU'. That plausibly points to the Montpellier university computing centre CNUSC with a CRAY-2 link. The CRAY-2 was only introduced in 1985, so this sheet (or at least the paper) may postdate the 1983-1984 dating of cote 154.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could refine the chronology of the pseudo-line notes: they may extend to 1985 or later, or this sheet may have been inserted later. This is relevant to dating Grothendieck's work on pseudo-line systems relative to Ringel, Goodman–Pollack and Manin–Schechtman.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a routine telescoping identity serving an orientation-monodromy check, plus rough sketches. The only mildly notable item is the CRAY-2 printout, which may bear on dating.
transcription_corrections: The line after 'ρ_1ρ_2 = σ_0σ_2' likely continues 'ρ_1ρ_2ρ_3 =' (telescoping), not 'ρ_2ρ_3 ='.
The line read as 'ρ_i^2 = 1 [?]' is more plausibly 'ρ_1…ρ_N = 1' (since σ_N = σ_0 and σ_i^2 = 1), followed by an illegible comment.
'Nadyu' is probably a name or annotation (unclear), not mathematics.
